passage: Early telescopes used glass lenses, which bend different colors of light by slightly different amounts, so their images were often blurred by colored fringes. To avoid this problem, Isaac Newton built a telescope that gathered light with a curved mirror instead of a lens. Because a mirror reflects all colors the same way, his design produced sharper images.
